programs.from_text: Curve value; Max limit; Min limit
programs.mechanism: Weather curve for L1 with both maximum and minimum supply-water limits.
programs.refute: The fitted max_c is above every supply the curve reaches, or min_c is below every supply the curve reaches.

programs.expr: clip(where(month() >= dry_start, base_c + slope * T_out + dry_add, base_c + slope * T_out), min_c, max_c)
programs.mechanism: Weather curve plus an autumn-only additive supply-temperature correction, still bounded by max and min limits.
programs.refute: The fitted dry_add is indistinguishable from zero, or the autumn window does not improve held-out room temperature.

programs.expr: clip(base_c + slope * lag(T_out, delay_h), min_c, max_c)
programs.mechanism: Weather curve driven by delayed outdoor temperature, with max and min supply limits.
programs.refute: The fitted delay_h is at the lower bound or the delayed curve does not improve held-out prediction over the undelayed curve.

programs.mechanism: Weather curve capped at a maximum supply-water temperature.
programs.refute: The fitted cap is above every supply the curve reaches.

programs.mechanism: Weather curve floored at a minimum supply-water temperature.
programs.refute: The fitted floor is below every supply the curve reaches.

programs.from_text: Two heating circuits, L1 and L2, one outdoor sensor
programs.mechanism: L2 weather curve using the shared outdoor sensor, with max and min supply limits.
programs.refute: L2 supply is better explained by no control or by a curve independent of the shared outdoor sensor.

programs.from_text: Floor heating. Kitchen also gets warm air rising from downstairs through the open space and balcony.
programs.expr: clip(base_c + slope * T_out + gain * (T_room - T_out), min_c, max_c)
programs.mechanism: L2 weather curve plus room-temperature feedback correction to counter the kitchen warm-air gain, bounded by max and min limits.
programs.refute: The fitted gain is indistinguishable from zero, or room feedback worsens held-out kitchen temperature.

not_expressible.from_text: The TV room radiator has an analog thermostatic valve, almost closed.
not_expressible.why: This is a local radiator valve action, not a supply-water setpoint law for the L1 loop; the language returns controller supply temperature, not valve position or room-level thermostatic modulation.
The absence of local thermostatic valves is plant context explaining why loop supply matters, but it is not itself a controller mechanism expressible as a supply-temperature program.

not_expressible.from_text: Indirect district heating substation; domestic hot water outside this controller.
not_expressible.why: These describe plant topology and scope, not a heating-circuit supply setpoint mechanism in the given signal language.
